facts_of_case: Appeal against respondents No.9-Dilip Kumar and respondent No.10-Jatan Singh has stood abated due to their death prior to 90 days.

legal_principles.principle: Once a party is impleaded, they cannot take a somersault and claim otherwise.
legal_principles.held: Respondents No.9 and 10 are estopped from taking a somersault and cannot claim that the sale deeds dated 28.06.2012 & 25.08.2011 executed in favour of respondents No.9 and 10 should be treated as nonest for the purposes of this appeal.
cited_cases: Surjit Singh And Others Vs. Harbans Singh And Others, (1995) 6 SCC 50

legal_principles.principle: A party cannot raise an objection that another party is not a necessary party if they themselves had impleaded the other party.
legal_principles.held: Once respondents No.9 and 10 have been impleaded on the application filed by appellants themselves, now, they are estopped from taking a somersault and cannot claim that the sale deeds dated 28.06.2012 & 25.08.2011 executed in favour of respondents No.9 and 10 should be treated as nonest for the purposes of this appeal.
cited_cases: Surjit Singh And Others Vs. Harbans Singh And Others, (1995) 6 SCC 50

outcome.final_order: The appeal would not stand abated as a whole, but only against respondents No.9 and 10.

use_for_drafting: drafting a second appeal in a property dispute case
advising on the implications of abatement in a family property dispute
guiding on the application of Hindu Marriage Act and Hindu Succession Act in a property dispute
